run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:25:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy warning is a downstream symptom. In the sampled window (default window 2026-11-18T00:25:06Z-01:40:19Z, span-rate samples 01:04Z-01:40Z), frontend-proxy's own error spans are only its server span 'ingress' and its client span 'router frontend egress', both http.status_code 500, i.e. 500 responses received from the frontend it proxies. The frontend's own error spans are gRPC calls to oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct returning status 14 UNAVAILABLE with 'No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080', which is exactly the product-catalog Service ClusterIP and port. At the same time Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (generation 4, revision 2) carried image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, which the kubelet cannot pull (401 UNAUTHORIZED, then ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff); the previously working ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) was scaled to 0 at 01:25:26Z, leaving the only product-catalog pod Pending and not ready, and the product-catalog Endpoints object holds only a notReadyAddress. product-catalog span traffic dropped to zero from the 01:31Z sample onward, and the consumers that call it (frontend, recommendation, checkout) each logged their own gRPC 14 errors against 100.69.9.250:8080. The single object holding the fault is the Deployment product-catalog. Who edited that Deployment, and exactly when, could not be observed because the change-history integration is not available.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error rate (sum by status_code, 5-minute rate) was 0 or at most about 0.011/s from the 01:04Z through 01:26:00Z samples, then rose to 1.30/s at 01:27:00Z, peaked at 13.15/s at 01:29:00Z, was 11.69/s at 01:36:00Z and 6.92/s at 01:40:00Z; concurrently STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate fell from about 20-23/s to about 8.5-8.9/s. This is the deviation the RequestErrorRate alert reflects.

Only two frontend-proxy operations carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans: 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client). Both are recorded with http.status_code 500; at the 01:36:00Z sample 'ingress' was 5.86/s and 'router frontend egress' 5.86/s, and no other frontend-proxy operation shows errors.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans show the proxy's 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans at http.status_code 500 with otel.status_code ERROR, and visible parent references link the egress span to the same trace's ingress span (trace 30fbe678a15611eefae6da638e0232ba: fed4b9933f623db7 to ca057e19807255e2), i.e. the proxy reports the 500 it received rather than failing in its own process.

The frontend service has its own error-span rate, larger than frontend-proxy's: 0.78/s at 01:27:00Z, 13.41/s at 01:29:00Z, 23.67/s at 01:31:00Z and 18.20/s at 01:39:00Z, so the frontend is where the failures are generated.

Frontend error spans name the failing dependency: operation 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080 - Local (0.0.0.0:0) (2025-12-15T17:59:02.649Z)' (exception.type 14), whose visible parents are the erroring 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]', 'GET /api/products/{productId}' and 'GET' spans, all http.status_code 500.

Frontend per-operation error rates (5-minute rate) for 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' were 2.69/s at 01:29:00Z, 4.76/s at 01:31:00Z and 4.41/s at 01:37:00Z; recommendation-related operations (grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, /api/recommendations) and checkout operations show smaller concurrent error rates, while GET and POST /api/cart, /api/data, grpc CartService and AdService show 0.

product-catalog's own span traffic stops: its STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate went 9.94/s at 01:27:00Z, 4.44/s at 01:29:00Z and 0 at every sample from 01:31:00Z through 01:39:00Z; no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned for product-catalog in that query, so it is observed failing by not serving rather than by returning error spans.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog is at generation 4 with annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision set to 2, and its pod template container 'product-catalog' image is 'quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0'; its status reports Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable and message 'Deployment does not have minimum availability', replicas 1 and unavailableReplicas 1.
A cluster-wide scan of 36 Deployments found exactly one whose pod template uses the hello-bench-invalid image: otel-demo/product-catalog.

Ownership chain: ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 (created 2026-11-18T01:25:18Z, image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, replicas 1 with no readyReplicas or availableReplicas in status) is owned by Deployment product-catalog, while the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, created 00:51:45Z) is now at replicas 0.

Events in otel-demo between 01:25:19Z and 01:30:49Z show the rollout and its failure: kubelet 'Failed' with message 'Failed to pull image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0": ... unexpected status from HEAD request to https://quay.io/v2/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid/manifests/1.0.0: 401 UNAUTHORIZED', plus ErrImagePull, ImagePullBackOff and BackOff on pods product-catalog-56fbb5f966-8rw7j and product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk (BackOff count up to 21); ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc recorded SuccessfulDelete and Deployment product-catalog recorded 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0' at 01:25:26Z and 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-56fbb5f966 from 0 to 1' at 01:25:34Z, and kubelet recorded Killing 'Stopping container product-catalog' on pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 at 01:25:26Z.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk is Pending with Ready=False (reason ContainersNotReady since 01:25:34Z), and its container 'product-catalog' is not started (restartCount 0) with state waiting reason ImagePullBackOff and message 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0": ErrImagePull: ... 401 UNAUTHORIZED'.

The address in the client errors is the product-catalog Service: Service otel-demo/product-catalog has clusterIP 100.69.9.250 and port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog, and the corresponding Endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses (IP 100.96.4.116, targetRef Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk) with no ready address.

recommendation is affected by the same dependency in its own spans: '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' has rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with otel.status_description 'failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:100.69.9.250:8080: connect: Operation not permitted (1)' (trace 06ff61df56fddca9d631ec5970f5dafa at about 01:36:03Z), and recommendation's error rate rose from about 0.004/s before to 1.65-1.77/s from 01:31:00Z.

checkout is affected by the same dependency: its span 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' is rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with otel.status_description 'connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.69.9.250:8080: connect: operation not permitted"', its 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' span is status 13 with 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"6E92ZMYYFZ"', and checkout's error rate was about 1.0/s from 01:31:00Z.

Feature-flag fault injection is not the trigger observed here: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (data key demo.flagd.json) has every flag at defaultVariant 'off', including 'productCatalogFailure' (description 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product') and the ad, cart, payment and recommendation flags, all with state ENABLED and the off variant selected as of the query.

Checked and healthy on the pod listing: all other otel-demo pods are Running, ready with restartCount 0, including the alerting service's pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-zj87n and the consumer pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-gx54w; only product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk is Pending. The frontend-proxy pod is therefore up while returning 500s, and its failure evidence is its own error spans, not a restart or readiness problem.

accounting and payment show STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0 at every sample from 01:05Z to 01:39Z, and ad and fraud-detection only show sporadic values of about 0.0037-0.0042/s that also appear before the deviation (frontend-proxy's own pre-incident baseline was the same about 0.0037-0.011/s); these are background, not part of this incident.

Rejected: a flagd feature-flag fault (for example productCatalogFailure) caused the product-catalog outage. The productCatalogFailure flag reads off in flagd-config, the change that removed the working product-catalog pod is an unpullable image in the Deployment pod template rather than a flag change, and product-catalog produced no error spans while its spans stopped entirely.

The connect failures surface as EPERM, 'connect: Operation not permitted (1)', rather than a plain connection refusal, which indicates the TCP connect was rejected at the network layer. The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no objects, so whether an additional network-layer block exists is unconfirmed; what is confirmed is that the product-catalog Service held only a notReadyAddress at that time, so clients had no ready backend.

Roll Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog back to a pullable image (ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc carried ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) and confirm the new pod reaches Ready so the product-catalog Endpoints object regains a ready address; then re-check the frontend, recommendation and checkout gRPC 14 error rates and the frontend-proxy ingress and egress 500 rates.

Add pre-rollout validation that the product-catalog image is pullable (quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 answers the manifest HEAD request with 401 UNAUTHORIZED) and alert on kubelet Failed and ImagePullBackOff events for otel-demo workloads, so a rollout that removes the last ready replica is caught before the error rate in frontend-proxy rises.

gaps: What changed the Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog pod template to quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, by which actor and mechanism and at which exact time, is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run. The change is bounded only by evidence timestamps: new ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 created 2026-11-18T01:25:18Z, its first pod Scheduled 01:25:19Z, the old ReplicaSet scaled to 0 and old pod killed 01:25:26Z, the new pod Scheduled 01:25:34Z. The alert start 01:25:06Z does not exactly match any observed object event.

The Deployment change is before the first non-zero 5-minute error-rate sample at 01:27:00Z, but the earliest retained per-request error spans examined are at about 01:36:03Z, so the exact first failing request time is unknown; no per-request trace sample between 01:25Z and 01:36Z was examined.

Application logs could not be used as evidence: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-gx54w returned no lines for 01:20Z-01:38Z (0 lines read from the current container, and the previous instance did not exist), and the product-catalog containers never started (ImagePullBackOff) so they have no logs. The old product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 was deleted at 01:25:26Z and its logs are no longer available.

No kube-state-metrics series are present for this target: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for namespace otel-demo and deployment product-catalog returned no data, so workload state over time was taken from the Kubernetes API state at query time and from events, not from metric history.

The otel-demo NetworkPolicy query returned no objects and the otel-demo ResourceQuota query returned no objects; these empty results are unknown rather than proof of absence, so an additional network-layer cause for the EPERM connect errors cannot be confirmed or excluded.

A coincident change during the window that is not tied to this cause: the flagd Deployment has a newer ReplicaSet flagd-9bbb84574 whose pod flagd-9bbb84574-hwqzz started 2026-11-18T00:53:26Z, while flagd-c47676d99 is at replicas 0, with the same two images in both ReplicaSets (ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8 and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-flagd-ui). This restart with an unchanged pod template is about 32 minutes before the product-catalog rollout, no evidence ties it to the errors, and what triggered it is unknown.
Whether product-catalog itself crashed or restarted before this rollout is unknown; only its current pod and the events inside the authorized window were readable.
next_steps: Use the not integrated change history to identify which principal or controller edited Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 around 2026-11-18T01:25Z.

After a human restores the product-catalog image, verify pod readiness and the product-catalog Endpoints ready addresses, then re-check the frontend, recommendation and checkout gRPC 14 rates and the frontend-proxy ingress and egress 500 rate.

If the EPERM connect errors persist after product-catalog has ready endpoints, review CNI and NetworkPolicy configuration for client pods (frontend, recommendation, checkout) reaching the product-catalog ClusterIP 100.69.9.250 on port 8080.
